text:
Ava: quick idea: let's add a tiny 'intake mini-probe' before models hit the full bench. goal = fast blocks for obvious incompat and flag lightweight regressions.
Diego: sounds good. what are the minimal signals we need?
Ava: thinking: (1) signature match, (2) binary compatibility, (3) tiny perf check (p90), (4) functional smoke on 8 examples.
Priya: keep samples small — 8 is fine. add a deterministic seed so runs are reproducible.
Ethan: how do we represent compatibility? we need codeable reasons so pipeline rules can act.
Ava: propose `compat_reasons` list with enums like: SIGNATURE_MISMATCH, UNSUPPORTED_OPS, QUANT_NONDET, RUNTIME_CRASH. plus human message.
Nora: where do we store the golden cases? registry-artifact ref or a shared bench bucket?
Priya: registry-artifact_ref is better; it ties to model version. bench can cache.
Diego: runtimes differ (cpu/gpu/quant). add `target_runner` in probe request and `matched_runner` in response. if no match, return best-effort with reason UNAVAILABLE_RUNNER.
Ava: good. probe request sketch: `probe_request = {model_id, target_runner, samples=8, seed, eval_suite_id?, warmup_prefix_len=0, timeout_per_sample_ms=3000, quick:true|false}`
Ethan: what's `quick`?
Ava: `quick=true` returns a sync short summary (pass/fail + p90) within a tight budget (200ms) if cached; otherwise it queues. UI can use this for preview.
Nora: result schema idea: single string payload in storage but shape: `status, compat, matched_runner, p50,p90,p99,per_case_deltas[],trace_id,artifacts[]`. keep it small.
Priya: include `golden_checksum` and `model_fingerprint` so we can audit.
Diego: what about KV cache warmup? some regressions only show after warm cache.
Ava: add `warmup_prefix_len`. default 0. teams can set to 1-3 to simulate warmed state.
Ethan: failure handling: categorize into HARD_BLOCK (signature, crash), SOFT_BLOCK (major perf regression), WARN (minor). pipeline rulebook maps to these.
Nora: mapping table please in RFC. also include manual override tag so teams can bypass with risk review.
InfraBot: quota note: mini-probe pool quota = 500 concurrent, max queued per team = 50. rate-limit 30/min/team.
Ava: include `priority` field: low -> mini-pool, high -> escalated bench; default low.
Priya: add `deterministic_output:true|false` to result to flag quantization nondeterminism.
Diego: for binary nondeterminism, return a `flakiness_score` 0..1 based on repeated runs. if >0.3 mark as flaky.
Ava: good call. also store short replay artifact: `replay_id` so infra can re-run with same RNG to debug. retention 14d.
Ethan: UX: ensure `probe_status` returns `state: queued|running|done|errored`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `retry_count`.
Nora: add `alert_level` computed: none|notice|page. attach to team on-call mapping.
Priya: small security note: probes must not exfiltrate golden content; enforce read-only artifact access and scrub outputs.
Ava: agreed. will add artifact scrubbing rules and an allowlist for eval-suite content.
Diego: action items: 1) Ava draft RFC with payload examples and rulebook by Tue.
Ethan: 2) I'll spin up a mini-probe shim that reads `probe_request` and returns a canned `result` for local testing.
Nora: 3) Priya will list common compatibility codes and recommended remediation steps.
InfraBot: feature flag required: `intake_mini_probe_v1`. enable in dev for testing.
Ava: cool. I'll drop the RFC link here when ready. thanks everyone.
Priya: quick Q: how do we handle models that purposely rely on nondeterminism (sampling)?
Ava: capture `sampling_mode` in metadata (deterministic|stochastic). for stochastic, compare eval-suite stats not exact strings.
Diego: ok that's a wrap. short and practical.
Ava: end.
